title: Short title, commencement and application
easy: Section 1 establishes the official title as Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita, 2023. It defines territorial jurisdiction across India and extra-territorial application to Indian citizens abroad.
takeaway: Names the Sanhita, sets its enforcement date (1 July 2024), and defines its jurisdiction.

title: Definitions
easy: Section 2 contains 39 statutory definitions including 'act', 'court', 'gender', 'good faith', 'injury', and new concepts like 'electronic records' to interpret the entire Sanhita consistently.
takeaway: Defines key legal terms and standardizes definitions across all criminal offences.

title: General explanations
easy: Section 3 provides rules of construction and 9 statutory explanations on common intention, joint liability, words expressing acts including illegal omissions, and liability for combined actions.
takeaway: Establishes statutory principles for interpreting liability, acts, and intentions.

title: Punishments
easy: Section 4 lists the six categories of legal punishment: death penalty, life imprisonment, rigorous/simple imprisonment, forfeiture of property, fine, and introduces community service.
takeaway: Lists the six statutory punishments under BNS, adding community service for minor offences.

title: Commutation of sentence
easy: Section 5 empowers the appropriate Government to commute any sentence to a lesser punishment without the consent of the offender, in accordance with Section 474 of BNSS, 2023.
takeaway: Authorizes Government to commute or reduce criminal sentences without offender consent.

title: Fractions of terms of punishment
easy: Section 6 provides mathematical rules for calculating fractional terms of punishment, specifying that life imprisonment is calculated as twenty years for fraction computation.
takeaway: Fixes life imprisonment at 20 years solely for computing fractional sentence terms.

title: Sentence may be (in certain cases of imprisonment) wholly or partly rigorous or simple
easy: Section 7 allows the court to sentence an offender to imprisonment that is partly rigorous (with hard labour) and partly simple, depending on gravity and justice.
takeaway: Gives courts discretion to combine rigorous and simple imprisonment in a single sentence.

title: Amount of fine, liability in default of payment of fine, etc
easy: Section 8 regulates sentence of fine, proportionality to offender's means, and specifies that fines must not be excessive even where no express maximum limit is prescribed by law.
takeaway: Requires fines to be reasonable, non-excessive, and proportionate to means.

title: Limit of punishment of offence made up of several offences
easy: Section 9 governs imprisonment in default of payment of fine, limiting the default term to not exceed one-fourth of the maximum term of imprisonment fixed for the offence.
takeaway: Restricts default imprisonment for non-payment of fine to one-fourth the maximum sentence.

title: Punishment of person guilty of one of several offences, judgment stating that it is doubtful of which
easy: Section 10 sets the maximum default imprisonment scale when the offence is punishable with fine only: from 2 months up to a maximum of 6 months based on the fine amount.
takeaway: Provides a graded scale for default imprisonment when an offence carries only a fine.

title: Solitary confinement
easy: Section 11 provides that default imprisonment terminates immediately upon full payment of the fine, or prorated early upon proportional payment of the unpaid balance.
takeaway: Default imprisonment ceases promptly upon full or proportional payment of fine.

title: Limit of solitary confinement
easy: Section 12 regulates solitary confinement, restricting it to rigorous imprisonment cases, capped at maximum 3 months total, and ordered in short intervals to prevent cruelty.
takeaway: Limits solitary confinement to rigorous imprisonment with strict maximum time caps.

title: Enhanced punishment for certain offences after previous conviction
easy: Section 13 restricts execution of solitary confinement to not exceed 14 days at a time with equal non-solitary intervals, and maximum 7 days per month for longer sentences.
takeaway: Enforces mandatory intervals and periodic caps during solitary confinement execution.

title: Act done by a person bound, or by mistake of fact believing himself bound, by law
easy: Section 14 provides that an act done by a person who is bound by law, or who by reason of mistake of fact in good faith believes himself bound by law, is not an offence.
takeaway: Protects acts done under legal duty or genuine good-faith mistake of fact.

title: Act of Judge when acting judicially
easy: Section 15 protects judicial officers, providing that nothing is an offence which is done by a Judge when acting judicially in exercise of power given or believed in good faith to be given by law.
takeaway: Confers complete criminal immunity on judges acting within judicial jurisdiction.

title: Act done pursuant to judgment or order of Court
easy: Section 16 protects ministerial officers executing court orders or warrants, provided the act is done in good faith pursuant to a court judgment or order in force.
takeaway: Shields officers carrying out valid court judgments, warrants, or orders.

title: Act done by a person justified, or by mistake of fact believing himself justified, by law
easy: Section 17 protects acts justified by law, or done by a person who by reason of mistake of fact in good faith believes himself to be justified by law in doing it.
takeaway: Exonerates acts justified by statutory law or reasonable mistake of fact.

title: Accident in doing a lawful act
easy: Section 18 provides complete defence for pure accident: acts done without criminal intention or knowledge in the doing of a lawful act in a lawful manner with proper care and caution.
takeaway: Excludes criminal liability for unavoidable accidents occurring during lawful acts.

title: Act likely to cause harm, but done without criminal intent, and to prevent other harm
easy: Section 19 codifies the doctrine of necessity: an act done without criminal intent to cause harm, in good faith to prevent other greater harm to person or property, is protected.
takeaway: Protects acts causing lesser harm to avert an imminent greater catastrophe.

title: Act of a child under seven years of age
easy: Section 20 establishes absolute criminal immunity for infancy: nothing done by a child under seven years of age can be constituted as an offence under the law (doli incapax).
takeaway: Grants absolute defence of infancy for all children under the age of 7 years.

title: Act of a child above seven and under twelve years of age of immature understanding
easy: Section 21 provides qualified defence for children aged 7 to 12 who have not attained sufficient maturity of understanding to judge the nature and consequences of their conduct.
takeaway: Protects children aged 7-12 who lack maturity to understand conduct consequences.

title: Act of a person of unsound mind
easy: Section 22 codifies the legal insanity defence (McNaghten rule): acts done by persons of unsound mind unable to know nature of act or that it is wrong or contrary to law are not offences.
takeaway: Exempts persons of unsound mind who cannot discern right from wrong or act nature.

title: Act of a person incapable of judgment by reason of intoxication caused against his will
easy: Section 23 protects involuntary intoxication: acts committed by a person intoxicated against their will or without knowledge, rendering them incapable of knowing the nature of the act.
takeaway: Exempts criminal acts caused by involuntary, forced, or unwitting intoxication.

title: Offence requiring a particular intent or knowledge committed by one who is intoxicated
easy: Section 24 clarifies liability for voluntary intoxication: where an offence requires specific knowledge or intent, the intoxicated person is judged as if having the same knowledge as when sober.
takeaway: Presumes normal sober knowledge for offences committed under voluntary intoxication.

title: Act not intended and not known to be likely to cause death or grievous hurt, done by consent
easy: Section 25 protects acts not intended or known to cause death or grievous hurt done by consent of an adult victim, commonly applied in sports, martial arts, and lawful games.
takeaway: Immunity for consensual lawful acts not intended to cause death or serious injury.

title: Act not intended to cause death, done by consent in good faith for person's benefit
easy: Section 26 protects medical and surgical acts: acts done in good faith for a person's benefit with consent, even if carrying risk of harm, provided there was no intent to cause death.
takeaway: Protects surgeons and doctors performing medical procedures with patient consent.

title: Act done in good faith for benefit of child or person of unsound mind, by, or by consent of guardian
easy: Section 27 enables guardians to give consent in good faith for medical operations or beneficial acts for children under 12 or persons of unsound mind.
takeaway: Validates parental or guardian consent for beneficial medical treatment of minors.

title: Consent known to be given under fear or misconception
easy: Section 28 clarifies what does not constitute valid consent: consent given under fear of injury, misconception of fact, or by intoxicated, insane, or child persons is invalid.
takeaway: Invalidates consent obtained through fear, deception, intoxication, or from children.

title: Exclusion of acts which are offences independently of harm caused
easy: Section 29 clarifies that consent cannot legalise acts that are offences independently of the harm caused to the consenting person, such as causing miscarriage or public nuisance.
takeaway: Consent cannot legalise acts that are inherently illegal under public criminal law.

title: Act done in good faith for benefit of a person without consent
easy: Section 30 protects emergency medical treatment done in good faith for a patient's benefit without consent when the victim is unconscious or unable to give immediate consent.
takeaway: Protects emergency medical procedures performed on unconscious victims without consent.

title: Communication made in good faith
easy: Section 31 protects professional communications made in good faith for a person's benefit, such as a doctor informing a patient of a severe medical prognosis.
takeaway: Shields truthful, good-faith warnings and professional medical communications.

title: Act to which a person is compelled by threats
easy: Section 32 codifies compulsion by threat: acts done under reasonable apprehension of instant death are excused, excluding murder and offences against the State punishable with death.
takeaway: Excuses acts compelled by immediate threat of death, excluding murder and treason.

title: Act causing slight harm
easy: Section 33 codifies the legal maxim 'de minimis non curat lex': acts causing harm so slight that no person of ordinary sense and temper would complain are not offences.
takeaway: Excludes frivolous or trivial complaints where harm caused is utterly negligible.

title: Things done in private defence
easy: Section 34 declares the fundamental statutory principle: nothing is an offence which is done in the lawful exercise of the right of private defence.
takeaway: Establishes that legitimate self-defence of person or property is not a crime.

title: Right of private defence of body and of property
easy: Section 35 sets out the scope of private defence: every person has a right to defend their own body and that of others, as well as movable and immovable property against crimes.
takeaway: Grants every citizen the right to defend human body and property against offences.

title: Right of private defence against act of a person of unsound mind, etc
easy: Section 36 affirms that the right of private defence exists equally against attacks by persons of unsound mind, intoxicated individuals, or children lacking legal capacity.
takeaway: Upholds private defence even against attackers who lack criminal capacity.

title: Acts against which there is no right of private defence
easy: Section 37 defines limits on private defence: no defence against acts of public servants acting lawfully, where time exists to seek police help, and force used must not be excessive.
takeaway: Prohibits self-defence against lawful public servant acts; forbids excessive force.

title: When right of private defence of body extends to causing death
easy: Section 38 lists 6 grave assaults where private defence of the body extends to causing death: murder risk, grievous hurt risk, rape, unnatural lust, kidnapping, and wrongful confinement.
takeaway: Allows lethal force in defence against murder, rape, grievous hurt, and kidnapping.

title: When such right extends to causing any harm other than death
easy: Section 39 provides that if the assault on the body is not of the 6 deadly categories in Section 38, private defence extends to causing any harm short of death.
takeaway: Restricts self-defence to non-lethal harm when assault does not threaten death/rape.

title: Commencement and continuance of right of private defence of body
easy: Section 40 specifies that the right of private defence of the body begins as soon as reasonable apprehension of danger arises, and continues as long as that apprehension exists.
takeaway: Self-defence starts with reasonable fear of danger and ends once danger ceases.

title: When right of private defence of property extends to causing death
easy: Section 41 specifies when defence of property extends to causing death: robbery, house-breaking by night, mischief by fire to buildings, and theft/mischief causing death apprehension.
takeaway: Authorizes lethal force to protect property against robbery, arson, and night burglary.

title: When such right extends to causing any harm other than death
easy: Section 42 provides that in cases of property offences not enumerated in Section 41, private defence extends to causing any proportionate harm other than death.
takeaway: Limits force to non-lethal harm during ordinary trespass, theft, or property damage.

title: Commencement and continuance of right of private defence of property
easy: Section 43 defines commencement and continuance of property defence: starts when danger begins, and continues until offender retreats, property is recovered, or police arrive.
takeaway: Property defence lasts until property is recovered, police intervene, or threat ends.

title: Right of private defence against deadly assault when there is risk of harm to innocent person
easy: Section 44 protects defenders who, while repelling a deadly assault, run the unavoidable risk of harming an innocent bystander, such as firing at a mob using children as shields.
takeaway: Protects necessary defensive actions even if risk of incidental harm to bystanders exists.

title: Abetment of a thing
easy: Section 45 defines abetment: instigating any person to commit an offence, engaging in a criminal conspiracy, or intentionally aiding by any act or illegal omission.
takeaway: Defines abetment through instigation, conspiracy agreement, or active assistance.

title: Abettor

takeaway: Defines essential legal boundaries and liability rules for abettor.

takeaway: Enforces strict criminal liability on individuals abetting or facilitating abetment in india of offences outside india.

title: Abetment outside India for offence in India

takeaway: Enforces strict criminal liability on individuals abetting or facilitating abetment outside india for offence in india.

easy: Section 57 sets out statutory provisions governing 'Abetting commission of offence by public or by more than ten persons' under Abetment, Conspiracy and Attempt of BNS 2023, clarifying legal boundaries, elements of offence, and liability.
takeaway: Defines essential legal boundaries and liability rules for abetting commission of offence by public or by more than ten persons.

title: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life
easy: Section 58 sets out statutory provisions governing 'Concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life' under Abetment, Conspiracy and Attempt of BNS 2023, clarifying legal boundaries, elements of offence, and liability.
takeaway: Defines essential legal boundaries and liability rules for concealing design to commit offence punishable with death or imprisonment for life.

title: Public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent
easy: Section 59 establishes statutory obligations, accountability standards, and legal penalties regarding public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent under public governance law.
takeaway: Enforces public integrity and accountability standards for public servant concealing design to commit offence which it is his duty to prevent.

title: Concealing design to commit offence punishable with imprisonment
easy: Section 60 sets out statutory provisions governing 'Concealing design to commit offence punishable with imprisonment' under Abetment, Conspiracy and Attempt of BNS 2023, clarifying legal boundaries, elements of offence, and liability.
takeaway: Defines essential legal boundaries and liability rules for concealing design to commit offence punishable with imprisonment.

title: Criminal conspiracy
easy: Section 61 defines criminal conspiracy: when two or more persons agree to do an illegal act or an act by illegal means, punishable with imprisonment equal to abetment.
takeaway: Criminalizes agreement between two or more persons to execute unlawful acts.

title: Punishment for attempting to commit offences punishable with imprisonment for life or other imprisonment
easy: Section 62 penalizes attempts to commit offences punishable with imprisonment where no express attempt provision exists, awarding up to half of the longest prescribed term.
takeaway: Punishes uncompleted criminal attempts with up to half the full offence sentence.

title: Rape
easy: Section 63 defines the offence of rape comprehensively, detailing non-consensual sexual acts, penetration, and circumstances invalidating consent under BNS 2023.
takeaway: Defines rape and specifies legal conditions under which victim consent is void.

title: Punishment for rape
easy: Section 64 prescribes punishment for rape: rigorous imprisonment of not less than 10 years extending to life imprisonment, with fine directed to the victim for medical rehabilitation.
takeaway: Mandates minimum 10 years up to life imprisonment plus medical fine for rape.

title: Punishment for rape in certain cases

takeaway: Prescribes statutory prison terms and financial fines for punishment for rape in certain cases.

takeaway: Prescribes statutory prison terms and financial fines for punishment for causing death or resulting in persistent vegetative state of victim.

takeaway: Defines essential legal boundaries and liability rules for sexual intercourse by husband upon his wife during separation.

takeaway: Defines essential legal boundaries and liability rules for sexual intercourse by a person in authority.

title: Sexual intercourse by employing deceitful means, etc
easy: Section 69 introduces a specific BNS offence: penalizing deceitful promises to marry, false identity, or fraudulent inducement to engage in sexual intercourse with up to 10 years jail.
takeaway: Punishes sexual relations obtained through deceitful promises to marry up to 10 years.

title: Gang rape
easy: Section 70 penalizes gang rape: rigorous imprisonment for not less than 20 years extending to life (remainder of natural life) or death where victim is under 18 years.
takeaway: Mandates minimum 20 years up to natural life imprisonment or death for gang rape.

title: Punishment for repeat offenders

takeaway: Prescribes statutory prison terms and financial fines for punishment for repeat offenders.

takeaway: Defines essential legal boundaries and liability rules for disclosure of identity of victim of certain offences, etc.

title: Printing or publishing any matter relating to Court proceedings without permission

takeaway: Defines essential legal boundaries and liability rules for printing or publishing any matter relating to court proceedings without permission.

title: Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to outrage her modesty
easy: Section 74 penalizes assault or use of criminal force to any woman with intent to outrage her modesty, prescribing imprisonment from 1 to 5 years plus fine.
takeaway: Punishes outraging modesty of women with mandatory 1 to 5 years imprisonment.

title: Sexual harassment
easy: Section 75 defines and punishes sexual harassment, unwelcome physical contact, demands for sexual favours, or showing pornography with rigorous imprisonment up to 3 years.
takeaway: Penalizes unwelcome physical, verbal, or visual sexual harassment up to 3 years.

title: Assault or use of criminal force to woman with intent to disrobe
easy: Section 76 penalizes assault or use of criminal force with intent to disrobe or compel a woman to be naked, with mandatory rigorous imprisonment from 3 to 7 years.
takeaway: Strictly punishes assault aimed at stripping or disrobing a woman with 3-7 years jail.

title: Voyeurism
easy: Section 77 defines voyeurism: watching or capturing images of a woman engaging in private acts where privacy is reasonably expected, punishable with up to 3 to 7 years jail.
takeaway: Criminalizes recording, viewing, or publishing images of private acts without consent.

title: Stalking
easy: Section 78 defines and punishes stalking: physical following or monitoring a woman's internet, email, or electronic communications after disinterest is expressed.
takeaway: Punishes physical or electronic stalking and cyber monitoring of women up to 5 years.

title: Word, gesture or act intended to insult modesty of a woman
easy: Section 79 punishes words, sounds, gestures, or exhibition of objects intended to insult the modesty of a woman or intrude on her privacy with up to 3 years jail.
takeaway: Penalizes verbal insults, obscene gestures, and privacy intrusion against women.

title: Dowry death
easy: Section 80 codifies dowry death: death of a woman within 7 years of marriage by burns, bodily injury, or unnatural causes where dowry cruelty is shown, minimum 7 years to life.
takeaway: Prescribes minimum 7 years up to life imprisonment for dowry-related deaths.

title: Cohabitation caused by man deceitfully inducing belief of lawful marriage
easy: Section 81 sets out statutory provisions governing 'Cohabitation caused by man deceitfully inducing belief of lawful marriage' under Offences Against Woman and Child of BNS 2023, clarifying legal boundaries, elements of offence, and liability.
takeaway: Defines essential legal boundaries and liability rules for cohabitation caused by man deceitfully inducing belief of lawful marriage.

title: Marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife

takeaway: Defines essential legal boundaries and liability rules for marrying again during lifetime of husband or wife.

title: Marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage
easy: Section 83 targets deceptive practices involving marriage ceremony fraudulently gone through without lawful marriage, protecting innocent citizens from deceit, financial exploitation, and fraud.
takeaway: Protects citizens and businesses against deceptive schemes and financial trickery.

easy: Section 84 sets out statutory provisions governing 'Enticing or taking away or detaining with criminal intent a married woman' under Offences Against Woman and Child of BNS 2023, clarifying legal boundaries, elements of offence, and liability.
takeaway: Defines essential legal boundaries and liability rules for enticing or taking away or detaining with criminal intent a married woman.

title: Husband or relative of husband of a woman subjecting her to cruelty
easy: Section 85 penalizes cruelty by husband or relatives of husband toward a woman, including physical harm, mental harassment, or unlawful dowry demands with up to 3 years jail.
takeaway: Penalizes domestic cruelty, mental torture, and dowry harassment by marital family.

title: Cruelty defined

takeaway: Defines essential legal boundaries and liability rules for cruelty defined.

takeaway: Defines essential legal boundaries and liability rules for kidnapping, abducting or inducing woman to compel her marriage, etc.

takeaway: Defines essential legal boundaries and liability rules for causing miscarriage.

takeaway: Defines essential legal boundaries and liability rules for death caused by act done with intent to cause miscarriage.

easy: Section 91 sets out statutory provisions governing 'Act done with intent to prevent child being born alive or to cause to die after birth' under Offences Against Woman and Child of BNS 2023, clarifying legal boundaries, elements of offence, and liability.

title: Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide
easy: Section 92 sets out statutory provisions governing 'Causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide' under Offences Against Woman and Child of BNS 2023, clarifying legal boundaries, elements of offence, and liability.
takeaway: Defines essential legal boundaries and liability rules for causing death of quick unborn child by act amounting to culpable homicide.

title: Culpable homicide
easy: Section 100 defines culpable homicide: causing death by doing an act with intention of causing death, bodily injury likely to cause death, or knowledge of causing death.
takeaway: Defines culpable homicide as the foundational degree of unlawful human killing.

title: Murder
easy: Section 101 defines murder: culpable homicide committed with specific highest-degree malicious intention or reckless knowledge that death is the almost certain result.
takeaway: Defines murder as highest-degree intentional culpable homicide with no lawful excuse.

title: Culpable homicide by causing death of person other than person whose death was intended

takeaway: Defines essential legal boundaries and liability rules for culpable homicide by causing death of person other than person whose death was intended.

title: Punishment for murder
